newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on profit taking, technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on profit taking, technicals.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed lower on a profit taking technical slide with rain forecasts for portions of the drier U.S. Great Plains and signs of showers in key European wheat areas also mentioned, traders said.
Weather patterns suggested some potential relief for the crop in drier areas of the U.S. and in France.

Weather Services Corp early Thursday predicted showers in the northern and western portions of the U.S. Southern Plains. Portions of the U.S. Plains states need additional rainfall to boost crop production potential.
England and France can expect Thursday's warm, dry weather to continue into the weekend but rain is forecast for Sunday, Weather Services Corp said.
Forecasts for colder weather by the weekend in Ohio and portions of Missouri failed to stir the market, they said.

USDA's weekly export sales report underpinned prices. USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended April 24 totaled 290,500 tonnes, above trade expectations for 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to nine cents per bushel lower, with July down nine 8-1/2 cents at $4.25.
In spread trading, Gelber Trading did 600,000 bushels of July/May at 11 cents, premium July and USA Trading did 400,000 July/September at 5-1/2 cents, premium September, traders said.

In outright trading, Merrill Lynch Futures, O'Connor and Co, Rand Financial and Continental Grain each sold roughly one million bushels of July, traders said. Refco Inc sold 1.5 million bushels of July and Cargill Inc was a late seller of 1.5 million July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 20,000 contracts, slightly below the 20,989 traded Wednesday.
In wheat options, Farmers Commodities Corp sold 225 July $4.30 puts at 19 cents, Term Commodities bought 200 July $4.00 puts at 7-1/4 cents and sold 200 July $3.80 puts at 3-1/4 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,500 contracts, above the 7,107 traded Wednesday.
